deep.reconstruction:
This page holds no mathematical derivation. It is a financial or statistical ledger written in Gauss's hand, with consistent pen changes suggesting it was updated year by year up to 1854.

(1) Annual table, 1835–1854, with two money columns. The amounts are written as Thaler.Groschen(.Pfennig). The arithmetic below shows 24 Groschen to the Thaler (e.g. 18 + 12 Gr = 1 Th 6 Gr), as in the Hanoverian or Conventions reckoning. The figures in each column fluctuate around 180–310 Thaler a year. For 1835–1841 only, a third column of small integers appears (5, 5, 8, 11, 6, 3, 3), perhaps counts of some item. What the two columns record (e.g. receipts vs. expenditure, two funds, or two sources of income) is not stated. Context does not decide it; the adjacent pages hold optics notes, a Goethe quotation and a list of the Pour le mérite order.

(2) 'Je 7 Jahre' (every seven years). The years are summed in blocks of seven: 1800–06, 1807–13, 1814–20, 1821–27, 1828–34, 1835–41, 1842–48. The marks 'Cass' and 'Cour' bracket the first three blocks and the next two. They most plausibly mean that those sums are in Cassengeld (Kassenmünze) and Courant respectively, i.e. two different currency standards.

Verification (mine), working in Groschen with 24 Gr = 1 Th:
- 1835–41, column 1: 287 + 243 + 222 + 309 + 179 + 211 + 217.12 = 1668.12. This matches Gauss's '35–41 1668.12.0'.
- 1835–41, column 2: 265 + 274.18 + 306.12 + 192.12 + 201 + 242 + 262 = 1743.18. Matches.
- 1842–48, column 1: 228.6 + 189 + 223.6 + 205 + 180.12 + 181 + 178.12 = 1385.12. Matches.
- 1842–48, column 2: 211.18 + 227 + 206 + 199.12 + 201.6 + 184.20 + 253 = 1483.8. Matches.

The earlier blocks (1800–1834) cannot be checked, because their annual data are not on this page. The 1821–27 block (3074.6.4 / 3429.2.0) is roughly twice the size of the other blocks; why is not explained.

(3) Continuation, 1850–1854: single years only. 1853 has no second-column entry and 1854 has no first-column entry.

Purpose: tracking a long-run personal or institutional money series, perhaps looking for trends or cycles by seven-year aggregation. This is routine bookkeeping arithmetic.
errors: No arithmetic errors detected in the checkable seven-year sums (1835–41 and 1842–48 both agree exactly in base-24 Groschen).
The 1800–1834 block sums cannot be verified from this page.

results.what: Seven-year aggregated sums of annual monetary amounts (Thaler/Groschen/Pfennig, 24 Gr = 1 Th), with currency standard noted (Cassengeld vs Courant)
results.modern_name: Bookkeeping / block aggregation of a time series (non-overlapping 7-year totals)

deep.surprise_reason: Purely a personal or administrative financial ledger with correct mixed-radix additions. There is no mathematical novelty; Gauss's habit of keeping such statistical and financial tables is well known.

checkable.asserts: 1842–48 first-column total equals 1385 Th 12 Gr (result 0), confirming 1847 entry is 181.0

transcription_corrections: 1847 first column reads 181.0 (the overwritten digit is 0); confirmed by the 42–48 sum 1385.12.
The '?' after 1843's 227.0 is a small superscript mark (looks like '2'), not a question mark.
The small annotation above 1845's 205.0 reads 'Je 7' (anticipating 'Je 7 Jahre').
'Cass' and 'Cour' in the bracket notes very likely abbreviate Cassengeld (Kassenmünze) and Courant, i.e. the currency standard of the block sums.
